title: Variational Cross-Graph Reasoning and Adaptive Structured Semantics Learning for Compositional Temporal Grounding
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence

problems.name: Multi-Moment, Compositional, and Complex Query Grounding
problems.evidence_sentence: To systematically benchmark the compositional generalizability of temporal grounding models, we introduce a new Compositional Temporal Grounding task and construct two new dataset splits, i.e., Charades-CG and ActivityNet-CG.

problems.name: Domain Shift and Generalization
problems.evidence_sentence: A natural solution to this problem is to utilize the systematic compositionality [14], [9], [44] of human language, which enables us to form novel compositions by combining known words in novel ways to describe unseen activities (i.e., compositional generalization).

problems.name: Dataset, Benchmark, and Evaluation Mismatch
problems.evidence_sentence: To systematically benchmark the compositional generalizability of temporal grounding models, we introduce a new Compositional Temporal Grounding task and construct two new dataset splits, i.e., Charades-CG and ActivityNet-CG.

methods.name: Memory, Graph, or Structure Alignment
methods.evidence_sentence: Meanwhile, we introduce a novel adaptive structured semantics learning approach to derive the structure-informed and domain-generalizable graph representations, which facilitate the fine-grained semantic correspondence reasoning between the two graphs.

methods.name: Contrastive or Cross-Modal Alignment
methods.evidence_sentence: Based on this insight, we propose a variational cross-graph reasoning framework that explicitly decomposes video and language into hierarchical semantic graphs, respectively, and learns fine-grained semantic correspondence between the two graphs.
